summary: Add a notes feature for signed-in users. Users can create, list, read, edit and delete their own private text notes. Each note is bound to its owner and only the owner can access it.

features.name: Create note
features.description: A signed-in user saves a new private text note owned by them.

features.name: List and read notes
features.description: A signed-in user lists and views only their own notes.

features.name: Edit and delete note
features.description: A signed-in user updates or deletes only their own notes.

requirements.text: All notes endpoints require an authenticated session.
requirements.testable_check: Call each notes endpoint without a session; expect 401 and no data returned.

requirements.text: Each note stores its owner id, taken from the session, never from client input.
requirements.testable_check: POST a note with an extra owner_id field for another user; the stored note belongs to the session user.

requirements.text: A user can read a note only if they own it.
requirements.testable_check: User B requests GET on user A's note id; expect 404 or 403 with no note content.

requirements.text: A user can update or delete a note only if they own it.
requirements.testable_check: User B sends PUT and DELETE for user A's note; expect 404 or 403 and the note is unchanged.

requirements.text: The list endpoint returns only the caller's notes.
requirements.testable_check: Users A and B each create notes; A's list contains none of B's notes.

requirements.text: Note text is validated: it must be a string, non-empty, and within a maximum length.
requirements.testable_check: POST empty, non-string and oversize bodies; expect 400 and nothing stored.

requirements.text: Note content is output-encoded or returned as JSON/plain text so stored markup cannot execute.
requirements.testable_check: Save a note containing <script>; the response has a non-HTML content type or the page renders it as inert text.
Send SQL metacharacters in note text and id; expect no error and no data leakage.

requirements.text: State-changing requests are protected against CSRF when cookie sessions are used.
requirements.testable_check: POST a note from a cross-origin request without the CSRF token; expect rejection.

requirements.text: Security events (denied access, auth failures) are logged without note content.
requirements.testable_check: Trigger a cross-user access attempt; the log has user id, note id and outcome but not the note text.

requirements.text: Note ids are not guessable, or access control does not rely on id secrecy.
requirements.testable_check: Enumerate ids as another user; all return 404 or 403.

abuse_cases.attacker_goal: Plant a note under another user's account or inject script.
abuse_cases.steps: Send a create request with a forged owner_id or HTML/script content, or without a CSRF token.
abuse_cases.mitigation: Take owner from the session, validate input, encode output and enforce CSRF protection.

abuse_cases.steps: Change the note id in GET requests, enumerate ids, or call the list endpoint without a session.
abuse_cases.mitigation: Require auth and filter every query by owner id; return 404 for notes the caller does not own.

abuse_cases.attacker_goal: Modify or delete another user's notes.
abuse_cases.steps: Send PUT or DELETE with a victim's note id, or include an owner_id field to reassign a note.
abuse_cases.mitigation: Check ownership on every write, ignore client-supplied owner fields and log denied attempts.

open_questions: Which existing authentication and session mechanism does the app use (cookies or tokens)?
What are the maximum note length and any per-user note limit?
Should notes be encrypted at rest beyond standard database protection?
Should deleting a user account also delete their notes?
